extracted.intended_audience: researchers interested in participating in ASAPbio's crowd preprint review (potential reviewers and crowd leads)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for coordinating and participating in ASAPbio's community-based public reviews of preprints: reviewers join discipline-specific crowds, comment collaboratively (Google Doc) over a 14-day window, and produce a consolidated, section-wise synthesized public report attached to the preprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection / participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are *not* required to comment on every preprint — choose based on expertise and availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selective participation is encouraged rather than penalized; reviewers should opt in when the preprint falls within their wheelhouse and when they have time to contribute meaningful comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission platform
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are submitted via a collaborative Google Doc over 14 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the shared Google Doc as the working space for discussion and commenting; this is the official submission vehicle for the crowd review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframe for review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review activity is time-bounded: contributors should add their comments within the 14-day window allocated for each preprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may comment on the full paper or specific parts based on their knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors may focus on sections or issues matching their expertise (methods, data, interpretation, figures, etc.) rather than attempting to review the entire manuscript if outside their competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output format: consolidated section-wise synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are consolidated by section for ease of reading and posted as a public review attached to the preprint. The "report" is a synthesis, not an individual review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final product is a synthesized, section-organized report representing the crowd's collective input; individual comments are integrated rather than presented as separate signed reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination by crowd leads
rubrics_metrics.description: Crowd leads coordinate groups within a discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated crowd leads organize participants, manage the collaborative document/process, and help steer the group discussion within a given discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASAPbio support & logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: ASAPbio provides "a guide and support for logistics" to crowd leads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASAPbio supplies procedural guidance and logistical support (e.g., templates, procedures) to help crowd leads run reviews; crowd leads are not expected to invent the process from scratch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer training model
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers learn through participation in the collaborative process (no formal training course).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program relies on experiential, peer-learning: new reviewers gain skills by joining and contributing rather than through a structured training curriculum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Norm of public, named, collaborative review
rubrics_metrics.description: Public, named, collaborative review is treated as a legitimate alternative to closed journal review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are public and attributed, and the model positions this openness and collaboration as an accepted and valid form of peer evaluation distinct from traditional closed peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary scope / applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Current Disciplines: Cell biology preprints. Meta-research preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is currently implemented in specific disciplines (cell biology and meta-research); applicability to other fields may depend on crowd formation and community uptake.
